source.author: verg
source.text: hic crudelis amor tauri, suppostaque furto Pasiphaë, mixtumque genus prolesque biformis Minotaurus inest, Veneris monumenta nefandae; hic labor ille domus et inextricabilis error; magnum reginae sed enim miseratus amorem Daedalus ipse dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, caeca regens filo vestigia.
source.text_original: hic crudelis amor tauri, suppostaque furto / Pasiphaë, mixtumque genus prolesque biformis / Minotaurus inest, Veneris monumenta nefandae; / hic labor ille domus et inextricabilis error; / magnum reginae sed enim miseratus amorem / Daedalus ipse dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, / caeca regens filo vestigia.
source.text_english: Here is the cruel love of the bull, and Pasiphaë brought under by stealth, and the mixed breed, the two-formed offspring Minotaurus, memorials of shameful Venus; here is that toil of the house and the inextricable error; but Daedalus himself, pitying the queen’s great love, untangled the deceits and labyrinthine windings of the building, guiding the blind footsteps with a thread.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Abyssus abyssum invocat, in voce cataractarum Dei; et gyrans gyrando vadit spiritus, et in circulos suos revertitur: Labyrinthios patimur errores, et Christi caeca regimus filo vestigia.
reuse.text_original: Abyssus abyssum invocat, in voce cataractarum Dei; et gyrans gyrando vadit spiritus, et in circulos suos revertitur: Labyrinthios patimur errores, et Christi caeca regimus filo vestigia.
reuse.text_english: Deep calls to deep at the voice of God’s cataracts; and the spirit goes on turning in its turning, and returns into its own circuits: we suffer labyrinthine errors, and with the blind thread of Christ we guide our steps.
